transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2025-07-16
Start: 09:23 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Anika (CSM), Dr. Priya (Marigold Data), Carlos (Marigold BE), Rosa (Marigold PM), Sanjay (Marigold Sec), Jamie (Marigold SRE)

SUMMARY:
Quick sync on the token-affinity prefetch pilot: reviewed KV/prefix hit rates, observed burst eviction patterns overnight, discussed prompt-reuse vs user-session affinity tradeoffs, agreed on benchmark and config handoff.

TOPICS COVERED:
- Hit rate delta from baseline after initial prefetch rules
- Eviction churn during peak bursts and TTL tuning
- Prefetch cohorting (token-affinity) vs session-based affinity
- Telemetry gaps and what traces to share
- Security docs and next steps for benchmark and pilot extension

ACTIONS (brief):
- Redwood: updated config + cost delta, SOC2 + net diagram link
- Marigold: prod traces, list of critical prompt templates, confirm benchmark window

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone good morning, thanks for carving out time. Quick check — did the invite time work okay?
[00:13] Dr. Priya: Yeah works — sorry small delay from my side. Excited to see the hit‑rate numbers.
[00:30] Luca: Hi, Luca here. I pulled the latest from the pilot cluster, we have a few slides but i can also just share numbers. Is screen share okay?
[00:37] Carlos: Yep go ahead.
[01:02] Luca: Alright first slide real quick — baseline before prefetch was around 18–24% KV hit across the 3 app cohorts we were given. After we enabled token‑affinity prefetch with the 30s lookahead and cohorting rules, overall KV hit moved to 38–42% depending on the cohort. So roughly a +20pp uplift.
[01:34] Rosa: That's promising, was that steady across the day or concentrated in some windows?
[01:44] Luca: It's uneven. daytime steady state sits near 40% but our telemetry flagged short spikes where eviction churn drove hits down to the low 20s for ~5–10 mins during user bursts.
[02:10] Jamie: those bursts — are they from batch jobs or concurrent interactive sessions? we have some nightly report jobs that hit similar keys.
[02:23] Dr. Priya: it's mixed. A lot of the bursty traffic is interactive — users opening long chart sessions that trigger multiple prompt variants. But we have a handful of backend processes that hammer prompts at midnight.
[02:41] Luca: Right, so two axes to tune: prefetch window and eviction policy. We currently prefetch on token affinity grouping and keep items for 60s TTL; eviction is LRU at the moment and the cache size was tuned conservatively.
[03:04] Maya: quick clarifying Q — when you say token‑affinity grouping, that means we bucket by first N tokens and then prefetch likely continuations, correct?
[03:15] Luca: Exactly. It's prefix hashing — we use the first 8 tokens fingerprint to choose a cohort and prefetch top‑k continuations we observed in training traces. That is distinct from session affinity where we'd tie to the user session vector.
[03:32] Carlos: What's the difference in hit patterns if we flip to session affinity?
[03:40] Luca: Session affinity tends to do better for long lived sessions with a lot of repetition — hit rates can jump another 5–8pp for those users, but across the entire user base it can actually hurt because cold sessions won't have history and prefetching is more speculative. Token‑affinity is more robust for heterogeneous short sessions.
[04:05] Rosa: So for Marigold long chart viewers we might want session affinity in combination, right?
[04:12] Luca: Exactly, we recommended hybrid: token‑affinity as default plus session sticky mode for workouts labeled as long‑lived. That reduces eviction churn because the session items get boosted.
[04:29] Dr. Priya: The eviction churn — can you show an example trace?
[04:35] Luca: Sure. (shares trace) Here you can see at 02:13:05 many prefetch keys were inserted, by 02:13:50 we hit a transient 3x increase in requests causing many prefetched items to be evicted before they had a chance to be used. TTL 60s was too short for that pattern.
[04:56] Jamie: So we could raise TTL? what's the cost implication?
[05:03] Luca: If we raise TTL to 180–300s for session‑boosted items we'll see more memory footprint. I crunched rough costs: at current traffic raising TTL to 3m for boosted cohort increases estimated memory footprint ~12% which in hosted mode maps to a projected cost delta of ~6–8% of cache spend. We'll give a formal estimate.
[05:31] Maya: And memory usage vs latency tradeoff? customers often prefer slightly higher memory to cut egress tokens.
[05:40] Luca: You reduce repeat generation which reduces per‑token GPU cycles; we've seen cost per 1k tokens down by 9–11% in similar pilots when hit rate improved that much. So net ROI can be positive even if cache spend nudges up.
[06:02] Dr. Priya: Any privacy or security surface for holding more prefetched tokens? Sanjay?
[06:09] Sanjay: Good Q — Marigold can't persist PII in the cache layer, but the pilot is already configured to strip/normalize PII before keys are generated. We need the SOC2 artifact and the network diagram to show where cache lives (private subnet vs public).
[06:27] Maya: We'll share the SOC2 PDF + network diagram today; I already pinged security. Luca will paste links.
[06:34] Luca: I'll drop links in the notes.
[06:38] Rosa: Back to hit patterns — what's the breakdown per prompt template? we have ~12 templates flagged critical.
[06:46] Luca: We instrumented per‑template keys. Top 3 templates account for 62% of the hits. Some of the low frequency templates rarely benefit. If you can share the list of your critical templates we can bias prefetch toward those.
[07:03] Dr. Priya: We'll upload the template list after the call. Expect it by EOD.
[07:09] Carlos: You mentioned telemetry gaps — what exactly do you need from us?
[07:16] Luca: Full request traces for ~72 hours: request id, timestamp, first 16 tokens of prompt (hashed for privacy), resulting key, and outcome (cache hit/miss). If you can't share tokens, hashed prefixes are fine. Also a sample of keys that were evicted during bursts.
[07:35] Jamie: We can provide hashed traces, will scrub PII. I need to confirm retention policies, but should be ok.
[07:41] Sanjay: confirm we keep data in our VPC and share with Redwood via presigned S3.
[07:47] Maya: Sounds good.
[08:00] Luca: One other observation: we saw a class of prompts where prompt‑reuse (the user reuses partial prompt blocks) caused near perfect reuse if we coalesce common suffixes. There's an easy win with coalescing identical trailing tokens before computing keys. That boosted a test cohort by another ~6pp.
[08:26] Rosa: Coalescing — does that add compute pre‑step? latency?
[08:32] Luca: Minimal — a few microseconds per request for fingerprinting, negligible compared to GPU token generation.
[08:41] Maya: Great. On benchmarking — we propose a 3‑phase plan: small synthetic load with replayed traces, a peak burst test with scaled synthetic clients, then a long‑tail run for 24 hours. Preferred window from Marigold?
[09:00] Dr. Priya: Weekend for peak test is best, our prod traffic is lowest saturday. We prefer July 22–23 for the heavy run.
[09:09] Maya: Noted.
[09:12] Luca: For the benchmark we'll enable an experiment flag for session affinity and boosted TTL for session cohorts. We'll compare baseline, token‑affinity only, and hybrid.
[09:24] Carlos: What metrics will you report? apart from KV hit, we want end‑to‑end p95 latency, token cost delta, and number of spoiled prefetches (prefetch but evicted).
[09:36] Luca: We'll report KV hit, prefix hit, p50/p95 latency, GPU token cost per 1k tokens, memory footprint delta, and number of evictions per minute.
[09:47] Rosa: Will you include a map of which templates improved most?
[09:50] Luca: Yes — per‑template delta.
[09:53] Dr. Priya: Quick question on model variants — if we fallback to a smaller quantized model during overload, does the cache key remain compatible?
[10:03] Luca: Good catch. Keys are model+prefix hashed. We currently stick to a canonical key namespace per model family. Fallback to a compatible variant is supported but keys must be mapped; we can automap for small‑delta variants. For large architecture changes we'd need a remap strategy.
[10:26] Sanjay: That mapping has compliance implications — we need logs for remap events.
[10:31] Maya: We'll enable remap audit logs in the pilot for you.
[10:36] Luca: Ok next item: eviction policy tuning — LRU currently, but a boosted LFU for session cohorts performs better in our tests. We can flip eviction policy per cohort.
[10:50] Rosa: Are these changes hot‑deployable or need cluster restarts?
[10:55] Luca: Hot configurable — no restarts for policy/TTL changes. Only structural changes like adding another cache tier need deployment.
[11:06] Jamie: What about dedicated vs hosted? if we move to dedicated we can increase memory cap, less noisy neighbors. How does that affect cost & performance?
[11:16] Maya: For Dedicated we give reserved capacity, predictable throughput and isolation, we can give you a cost delta separate from hosted. We can run the benchmark on both setups if you want.
[11:28] Carlos: Let's first tune hosted, then if needed evaluate dedicated.
[11:33] Dr. Priya: Agreed. Also ROI calc — can you show projected token cost improvement vs additional cache cost?
[11:41] Luca: We'll include that in the config handoff. My rough earlier number: 9–11% lower token spend with +6–8% cache cost for TTL increase, but we'll produce precise models.
[11:56] Rosa: Anything blocking the benchmark?
[12:00] Maya: two things — Marigold traces and confirmation of benchmark window. If SOC2 docs are required for the team, we'll send them today.
[12:09] Sanjay: Please do. Also can Redwood provide a short note on how keys are hashed (algorithm) for our compliance?
[12:17] Luca: We'll include the hashing algorithm (SHA256 prefix) and key namespace doc.
[12:23] Dr. Priya: Great. On the prefetch config — can you provide the JSON we should apply to the cluster so our SRE can review?
[12:31] Luca: Yes, we'll push a sample config in the notes and attach a diff with comments.
[12:36] Maya: let's recap and assign next steps.
[12:40] Rosa: sounds good.
[12:43] Maya: Redwood will — 1) share updated prefetch config + cost delta by Friday 7/18, 2) send SOC2 + network diagram to Sanjay by tomorrow, 3) provision a benchmark plan for July 22–23 and confirm instrumentation.
[12:58] Luca: Also I'll include per‑template biasing suggestions and a recommended TTL matrix for session vs default cohorts.
[13:06] Dr. Priya: Marigold will — 1) upload hashed 72h traces by 7/20, 2) send the list of 12 critical templates by EOD today, 3) confirm Saturday window for peak test and point person for bench runs.
[13:22] Sanjay: I'll review SOC2 and follow up if we need anything else.
[13:27] Jamie: I'll coordinate the traces export with Carlos.
[13:31] Carlos: noted.
[13:33] Maya: Any other questions?
[13:36] Rosa: One last thing — can you add a flag to disable prefetch for a given template in case we see regressions?
[13:43] Luca: Yes, per‑template flip is supported. We'll include it in the config.
[13:49] Maya: Okay thanks everyone. We'll send notes and links in the next couple hours. If anything urgent ping me in slack.
[13:58] Dr. Priya: Thanks all.
[14:01] Luca: Thanks.

(End of meeting)
